response.sql: WITH pp AS (SELECT b.player_id, p.bats, AVG(b.double) AS avg_doubles FROM batting_postseason b JOIN player p ON p.player_id = b.player_id GROUP BY b.player_id, p.bats), idx AS (SELECT player_id, bats, avg_doubles, avg_doubles * 1.0 / AVG(avg_doubles) OVER () AS idx FROM pp), g AS (SELECT player_id, bats, avg_doubles, idx, idx - AVG(idx) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS gap FROM idx) SELECT player_id, bats, avg_doubles, idx, gap FROM g ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST, player_id LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A record is a row in batting_postseason; the per-player average is AVG(double) over those rows, which skips NULLs. Players with no non-null doubles have a NULL average and sort last.
The overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-player averages across all players, not a mean over all rows.
The gap is the player's index minus the mean of the per-player indexes for the same batting hand. Players with a NULL bats value form their own group.
The join to player is an inner join, so postseason rows with no matching player are dropped.
Ties on the gap are broken by player_id, which the request does not specify.
